newsitem.title: GERMANY: VICTORIA - H1 PREMIUM INCOME 4.57 BLN.
newsitem.headline: VICTORIA - H1 PREMIUM INCOME 4.57 BLN.

text.p: German insurer Victoria Holding AG said on Wednesday that its first half premium income in 1997 was 4.57 billion marks, down from 4.65 billion marks in the first half of 1996.
However, the group said that an unchanged dividend payout of 28 percent for 1997 looked secure.
The group said that earnings in the group's individual business areas had shown positive growth and for the full year the group expected an improvement in overall earnings.
The group went on to say that it planned to hold an extraordinary general meeting on December 1 to discuss the formation of ERGO Versicherungsgruppe.
ERGO will be the holding company for a merged group resulting from the fusion of Victoria and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG to create Germany's second-largest insurer after Allianz AG.
Reinsurance giant Munich Re will be majority holder of ERGO, as the majority owner of Hamburg Mannheimer.
Victoria had premium income of 9.578 billion marks in 1996. Dividends in 1996 were 28 percent in 1996, while earnings per share were 51 marks.
Victoria offers all the main lines of life and non-life insurance and owns D.A.S. Allgemeine Rechtsschutz Versicherungs AG, Europe's largest legal protection insurer.
